Iridescent

/ir-ih-DESS-ent/ · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Iridescent means showing shifting, rainbow-like colors that seem to change depending on the angle from which they're viewed

Sunlight caught the iridescent sheen of the soap bubble just before it burst.

Worked Example

The bride chose a fabric that looked plain gray in the shop's fluorescent light but revealed flashes of purple, green, and gold the moment she stepped outside into direct sun.

The fabric wasn't dyed multiple colors — its surface simply bent light differently depending on the angle, which is precisely what makes something iridescent rather than just colorful.

How Iridescent Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

shimmering

shimmering: emphasizes a shifting, glimmering quality more broadly

opalescent

opalescent: specifically evokes the milky, colorful glow of an opal

prismatic

prismatic: stresses that light is being split into rainbow colors, as through a prism

Antonyms

dull

dull: reflecting no notable light or color at all

matte

matte: having a flat, non-reflective, single-toned surface

How Strong Is It? — shiny → shimmering → iridescent

shiny vs. iridescent

shiny vs. iridescent: A shiny surface simply reflects light brightly, without necessarily changing color.

shimmering vs. iridescent

shimmering vs. iridescent: A shimmering surface flickers as light moves across it, hinting at but not yet splitting into full colors.

Sort It Out

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — irid-

Root — irid-: rainbow (Greek iris/irido-)

Suffix — -escent

Suffix — -escent: becoming, beginning to show

Put it together

Put it together: "Iridescent" literally means "becoming rainbow-like" — irid- traces back to Iris, the Greek goddess of the rainbow, while -escent marks a quality that is emerging or developing.

Use the root in a new word: iris

Use the root in a new word: iris: The colored part of the human eye is called the iris, named for the same rainbow goddess as the word 'iridescent.'

Root Check

Word Choice

descriptive, literary

Iridescent is a vivid, mostly descriptive word used for surfaces that visibly shift color with the light — soap bubbles, oil slicks, hummingbird feathers, certain fabrics and shells — not for objects that are simply multicolored or painted.
